title: Chapter 21 — Panel-Ready and The Integration Craft
intro: The integrated kitchen as a system — millwork coordination and fit disciplines.

sections.title: Integration Is Coordination
sections.content:
A fully integrated kitchen — where appliances disappear behind custom panels — is the premium end of kitchen design. It requires flawless coordination between the appliance salesperson, the kitchen designer, the cabinetmaker, and the installer.

Your role is project manager. You need to confirm panel dimensions, hinge specifications, handle placement, and clearance requirements with the cabinet shop before the order is placed.

sections.title: The Cost of Getting It Wrong
sections.content:
A panel that does not fit is a delay measured in weeks — because custom panels are built to order. Getting measurements wrong means the customer waits with unfinished appliances sitting in their new kitchen.

Measure twice. Confirm with the cabinetmaker. Verify against the manufacturer's spec sheet. Then order. The extra hour of verification prevents weeks of frustration.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating integration knowledge, ask:

Does the salesperson coordinate with the full project team — designer, cabinetmaker, installer?
Do they verify panel specifications before ordering?
Do they manage integration projects proactively — or reactively when problems arise?
